title: Copilot Studio: block sharing of agents that embed maker credentials
summary: Hold: already-shared agents are incorrectly listed as outside scope even though later publishing can be blocked. The publishing explanation also omits the documented exception for unshared authenticated agents, and the sharing-limits PowerShell call includes prose that cannot be run as printed.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials is an environment-level Copilot Studio control that can detect unsafe credential use and block sharing or publishing.
claims.quote: The Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials setting is an environment-level control for Microsoft Copilot Studio agents. It lets administrators warn makers about unsafe credential use or block unsafe sharing.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A shared agent can use design-time maker credentials at runtime, allowing another user to act with the maker's permissions.
claims.quote: These embedded maker credentials are supplied at design time and can be used when the agent runs. If the agent is shared, another user might cause an action to run with the maker's access instead of their own.

claims.where: What's changing: unsafe-agent definition
claims.claim: Unsafe sharing requires a connection that disallows credential sharing and uses design-time credentials instead of individual user authentication.
claims.quote:
The agent uses at least one connection that doesn't allow credential sharing.
The connection uses credentials supplied at design time instead of asking each user to authenticate with their own credentials.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: An unsafe connection in a called flow or agent can make the calling agent unsafe as dependency-based enforcement becomes available.
claims.quote: As dependency-based enforcement becomes available, an unsafe dependency can cause the calling agent to be treated as unsafe for sharing.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Dependency-based enforcement can expand over time.
claims.quote: Dependency-based enforcement can expand over time. Include called agents and flows in your governance and testing process.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Not covered
claims.claim: Connections configured to use end-user credentials are not subject to this restriction.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.where: What's changing: Publishing is disabled while enforcement is active
claims.claim: Publishing is disabled whenever enforcement is active and an agent uses the maker's credentials at runtime.
claims.quote: For authenticated agents, an agent that you didn't share can publish successfully, while an agent you already shared with another user is blocked from publishing when enforcement applies.
claims.fix: Qualify the sentence: 'For channels where publishing distributes the agent without a separate Share action, maker user credentials can disable publishing. For authenticated agents, an unshared agent can publish successfully; an already-shared violating agent is blocked.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-sharing-controls-limits alongside the configuration article.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls row 3
claims.claim: The printed Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration call, including '(set bot-limitSharingMode, bot-maxLimitUserSharing or bot-authoringSharingDisabled)', is a sharing-limits PowerShell command.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api.call to 'Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration' and update the rendered table. Move the parenthetical out of code into the note: first retrieve the environment's governanceConfiguration, then update settings.extendedSettings using the cited Add-Member examples. For example, bot-limitSharingMode='ExcludeSharingToSecurityGroups' and bot-maxLimitUserSharing='20' restrict viewer sharing; bot-authoringSharingDisabled=True disables Editor sharing. The current '(set ... or ...)' is prose, not documented executable syntax.
